title: Yochanan ben Pinchas
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: As in Mishnah Shekalim 5:1, he was in charge of the seals in the Second Temple. Hyman cites Eliyahu Zuta, chapter 15, where Yochanan ben Pinchas says, “The seasonings of Babylonia: shunya … the seasonings of the coast” [printed wording]. Rabbi Akiva adds, “Also,” and so on. Hyman infers that he preceded Rabbi Akiva and suggests that he may have been the Temple official.

notes.text: The Aramaic proverb beginning הליתא דנבל שיניא remains untranslated because its wording and meaning have not been securely resolved. Akiva is the ordinary expansion of ר״ע.

The finite returned search did not locate the obscure Eliyahu Zuta proverb; that does not prove its absence. הליתא דנבל שיניא — הליתא דחבלא ימא is retained in transliteration rather than replaced by an invented maxim. The preceding כ in כשקלים means as in Shekalim. Akiva is a contextual expansion of ר״ע, with its title component left R'. Hyman's chronological inference from the order of statements, and his perhaps identification with the Temple seals official, remain his inferences rather than a newly established identity.

Hyman’s printed article reads תבליתא דבבל שוניא — תבליתא דחבלא ימא. The supplied Hebrew has different letters, retained in this edition. Wikisource’s Eliyahu Zuta 16 and the Sefaria Pirkei Derech Eretz addendum both name Yochanan ben Pinchas and give the longer comparison of seasonings. The Wikisource commentary marked י״י explicitly glosses the ingredients as seasonings and spices. The Mishnah names a seals official of the same name. The suggestion that the two passages refer to one person remains Hyman’s.
